items.title: In India, Anwar calls on Muslim scholars to master AI while safeguarding Islamic faith and moral values
items.summary: KERALAM (INDIA), Sept 14 — The Muslim world must embrace artificial intelligence (AI) and new technologies while ensuring that faith, moral values and Islamic heritage remain firmly preserved, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Speaking before around 2,000 attendees, including Islamic scholars and students, Anwar said Muslim scholars and societies could not afford to remain detached from the rapid development of AI and modern technology, as a lack of knowledge and understanding could leave them vulnerable to external influences. Anwar also stressed the importance of preserving the turath (Islamic scholarly heritage), saying the Muslim world should not lose sight of the Quran, Sunnah and works of prominent Islamic scholars while embracing new knowledge and technology.

items.title: Driver trapped and killed in eight-vehicle Kota Kinabalu pileup
items.summary: The 44-year-old victim, who was driving a Toyota Hilux, was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry (MOH) medical personnel. Jalan Lintas Fire and Rescue Station chief Assistant Senior Fire Officer Noor Sherriyana Bohari said the station received an emergency call at 6.33am before six personnel and a fire engine were dispatched to the scene. "Firemen used special rescue equipment to extricate the victim, who was trapped inside the vehicle.

items.title: Malaysia Smelting faces near-term earnings hit from RHT suspension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd is expected to post lower earnings in the near term following the temporary suspension of mining operations at its subsidiary, Rahman Hydraulic Tin (RHT), analysts said. Apex Securities Bhd estimated that the suspension, which lasted about 4.3 weeks, could reduce Malaysia Smelting's third quarter financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26) net profit by about RM11 million to RM12 million. "After accounting for Malaysia Smelting's 80 per cent equity interest in RHT, this translates into an estimated RM2.7 million reduction in company-attributable earnings per week of suspension.

items.title: Ex‑minister Jamil Khir claims trial over RM860m Tabung Haji funds channelled into Saudi real estate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Religious Affairs Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom today claimed trial to three charges of dishonestly causing Lembaga Tabung Haji to dispose of RM860,308,770.51 worth of funds to a Saudi real estate company. Jamil Khir, 65, was charged with committing the offences while serving as minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Religious Affairs in 2015, 2016 and 2017. The first charge alleges that Jamil Khir had, on April 3, 2015, at his office in the Prime Minister’s Department in Putrajaya, dishonestly caused Tabung Haji to dispose of RM42,942,074 to Al-Rawda Real Estate Development and Projects Management Co. Ltd.

items.title: Anwar receives inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award
items.summary: KERALAM (INDIA), Sept 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last night received the inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of his more than five decades of public service and contributions to education, Islamic scholarship, institutional development, international dialogue and human well-being. The award was presented to Anwar by Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, at the Gathering of Honour for the Prime Minister of Malaysia event at Markazu Saquafathi Sunniya, also known as Jamia Markaz here. “With profound respect that Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation confers upon Anwar Ibrahim the first Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of his distinguished contribution to public service, education, economic and institutional development, Islamic thought and international dialogue, as well as in honour of a life dedicated to shaping society through knowledge, leadership, and service to humanity,” he said.

items.title: Jamil Khir charged with causing TH to dispose of RM860.3mil assets
items.summary: Jamil Khir, 65, who was the minister in charge of religious affairs, pleaded not guilty to all three charges before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad. According to the charges, Jamil Khir allegedly caused TH to dispose of RM860,308,770.51, equivalent to SAR766,062,237, to Al-Rawda Real Estate Development And Projects Management Co Ltd. Under the first charge, he allegedly caused TH to dispose of RM42,942,074, equivalent to SAR44.17 million.

items.title: Former minister Jamil Khir appears in KL court over Tabung Haji RCI charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom arrived at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex here today to face charges related to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). According to the court system, the case against Jamil Khir is scheduled for mention before Sessions Court Judge Rosli Ahmad at 9am. On September 10, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said that the commission had recommended three charges against the former minister under Section 403 of the Penal Code for the offence of dishonest misappropriation of property.

items.title: Serian records country's worst API reading at 173
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IPD Serian recorded the country's highest air pollutant index (API) reading at 173 as of 8am today, remaining in the unhealthy category and showing little improvement from 174 yesterday evening. Meanwhile, 57 areas recorded moderate API readings as of 8am today, with Indera Mahkota, Pahang, recording the highest at 98. In Negri Sembilan, Port Dickson recorded 87, while Bukit Rambai and Bandaraya Melaka recorded 95 and 72 respectively.

items.title: Firemen rescue 14 trapped by surge of water in Sungai Pertak
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR: Firefighters rescued 14 people, including a child, after they were trapped in the middle of a river following a sudden surge of water at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Baru yesterday. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.03pm. He said a team of five personnel, along with a fire engine from the Kuala Kubu Bharu Fire and Rescue Station, was dispatched to the scene.

items.title: #NSTviral: Netizens pay tribute to Flying Doctors team after fatal crash
items.summary: Those were the words shared following the deaths of members of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) team who had dedicated themselves to providing medical care to communities in Sarawak's interior. The footage showed one of the victims, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, carrying out her duties as usual, including examining an elderly resident. "So heartbreaking to watch this video... Al-Fatihah to Dr Ainul and Captain Zainol... condolences to the families of the assistant medical officer, nurses Debra and Jessie," wrote Miea.

items.title: Anwar meets India’s Grand Mufti, discusses interfaith understanding and harmony
items.summary: KERALAM (INDIA), Sept 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held a meeting with the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, at Markazu Saquafathi Sunniya, also known as Jamia Markaz, in Calicut here yesterday, after attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. During the one-hour meeting, Anwar and Sheikh Abubakr exchanged views on community development, educational empowerment, and efforts to strengthen interfaith understanding and harmony. The Prime Minister, who arrived at 5.50pm local time with Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, was received by Jamia Markaz Working General Secretary Muhammad Abdul Hakkim Kandi, Director C.P.

items.title: Three shot dead, 15 wounded ahead of polls in Philippine Muslim enclave
items.summary: COTABATO, Philippines: Three people were killed and 15 others wounded as gunfire erupted hours before polls were to open Monday in a semi-autonomous Muslim region of the Philippines set to choose its first elected parliament. The vote is the culmination of an on-off peace process that began in the late 1990s and established the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in the country's far south. Cotabato police chief Jibin Bongcayao said the shooting took place just before midnight as members of rival political factions jostled for the right to cast their votes first.

items.title: Anwar to deepen Malaysia-India ties during Keralam visit
items.summary: Anwar will meet Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar. The prime minister will also hold one-on-one engagements with prominent Indian corporate figures to identify new trade, investment, and business opportunities in high-growth sectors. The engagements in Keralam complement Anwar's broader economic diplomacy in India, following the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi and his bilateral meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

items.title: "They see me, my face," Rehman on his viral moment with Anwar
items.summary: NEW DELHI: "I'm happy, very happy. My face, my face is being shown all around the world," said M.Rehman, who played the piano for Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim rendition of Kishore Kumar's classic "Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat." "On Friday, they told me Malaysian Prime Minister might come and that he is fond of Hindi songs.

items.title: Ex-minister Jamil Khir at KL Courts over Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom arrived at the Kuala Lumpur Courts Complex here this morning to face charges linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman last Thursday confirmed that a former minister would be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court today. He added that the MACC recommended three charges under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.

items.title: Beyond revenue sharing: Building the fiscal and institutional architecture of one Malaysian production economy
items.summary: Samirul Ariff Othman IF neighbouring states increasingly function as interconnected economic regions, Malaysia must confront a larger question - Does the country possess the fiscal and institutional architecture required to govern such an economy? Three Pillars Of Economic Federalism Malaysia needs to distinguish between three related concepts. Production federalism connects economic activity.

items.title: Analysts: Umno keeping 'strategic' options open ahead of GE16
items.summary: Universiti Malaya senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Umno was not buying time, as some may think. [[nid:1532237]] He said leaving the government now would carry significant risks, including losing these advantages and being perceived as a destabilising force. Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said there was now little doubt about where Umno was headed in terms of electoral cooperation.

items.title: Nestle Malaysia strengthens support for paddy farmers
items.summary: Faiqah Kamaruddin JITRA, Kedah: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has invested more than RM6 million in its Nestle Paddy Club (NPC) since 2012, as it seeks to strengthen its local rice supply chain while improving productivity and livelihoods among paddy farmers. Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the investment covers not only financial support but also farming methods, agricultural inputs, machinery and technical expertise. "Some farmers also take out paddy insurance.

items.title: Question over NorthEast's capacity constraint despite photonics opportunities coming its way
items.summary: Diyana Isamudin KUALA LUMPUR: NorthEast Group Bhd is still confident of chalking double-digit growth level for the financial year ending Sept 30, 2027 (FY27), as it secures more orders from its customers in the photonics, semiconductor and electrical and electronics (E&E) industries. The Penang-based precision engineering manufacturer is also confident of reaching record revenue for the current financial year ending Sept 30, 2026 (FY26), as it gains more orders from its existing customers. NorthEast manufactures mechanical systems and critical components used in photonics applications, including optical circuit switches (OCS), which facilitate high-speed data transmission in data centres.

items.title: Jet fuel surge adds RM7.5bil to MAG costs, Malaysia Airlines fares rise 30pct
items.summary: MAG group president and chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said every US$1 increase in oil prices affects the group's financial performance by about RM50 million. He said MAG was profitable in the first two months of the year before the sharp increase in fuel prices put significant pressure on operating costs. However, after the war began, fuel prices more than doubled.

items.title: Give SMEs a safe voice against cartels, MyCC urged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: enforcement powers for the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) must come with safe reporting channels, as small businesses often fear repercussions for complaining against major suppliers. [[nid:1532222]] Chin said educating small businesses is vital to effective enforcement, as small and medium enterprises (SMEs) face higher prices and unfair terms from cartels and dominant suppliers because of their weaker bargaining power. Chin said SMEs want competition based on price, quality and service.

items.title: MyCC: Stronger enforcement aims to protect fair competition
items.summary: Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) chairman Tan Sri Idrus Harun said the legal overhaul targets anti-competitive conduct such as cartels, price-fixing, market sharing, bid rigging and abuse of dominant positions that distort competition in the market. The 34-clause bill significantly expands MyCC investigative and enforcement capabilities. Idrus said strong and credible competition enforcement builds investor confidence by providing clear rules and ensuring enterprises compete on merit.

items.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched over 50 strikes against them in 24 hours
items.summary: SANAA: Yemen's Houthis said Sunday that Saudi Arabia had launched more than 50 strikes against their positions in 24 hours, after the Iran-backed group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom. The Houthis have been engaged in renewed fighting with Saudi-backed government forces since Yemen's civil war reignited in July, when the group declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea. The group's Almasirah TV channel reported on Sunday that "Saudi aviation carried out two strikes" on Saada, a stronghold for the group.

items.title: Stronger law gives MyCC edge against cartels [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Recent amendments to the Competition Act 2010 give the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) more powers and tools in the battle against cartels, bid rigging and price-fixing. MyCC chairman Tan Sri Idrus Harun said the amendments, which include expanded investigative powers, a settlement framework and a clear court appellate process, were essential to keep pace with evolving market tactics and sophisticated cartel operations. In July, the Dewan Rakyat passed the Competition Commission (Amendment) Bill 2026, which expands MyCC's powers, strengthens governance and enhances enforcement capabilities.

items.title: Malaysia’s AI Nation plan by 2030 — how the government is preparing its people
items.summary: Under the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030, Malaysia is targeting the creation of over 300,000 jobs attributable to AI by 2030. Basic digital and AI literacy The Digital Ministry’s Rakyat Digital platform provides free foundational learning in areas including AI, cybersecurity, cloud technology, blockchain and generative AI. Its AI-related courses include AI Fluency and Introduction to AI.

items.title: Oman says Hormuz talks with Iran, Gulf states postponed
items.summary: MUSCAT: Oman has announced the postponement of a meeting Monday between Iran and Gulf countries on the Strait of Hormuz, the major flashpoint in the Middle East war. Iran's foreign ministry had said there would be a meeting hosted by Oman where the future of the strait, vital for global oil and gas flows, would be negotiated. The Strait of Hormuz has been subjected to an Iranian and a later US blockade since February 28 when the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, prompting a wider war across the region.

items.title: Siti Farah battles financial hurdle to military dream
items.summary: TUMPAT: Three failed attempts at military selection have not dampened the determination of Siti Farah Damia Mohd Khairi, 20, to become a military officer. An offer to pursue a bachelor's degree in Defence Human Resource Management at Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) has given the former STPM student, who achieved a 3.67 cumulative grade point average, a chance to pursue her dream. Siti Farah has prepared only her daily clothing and basic necessities, though her Form 6 laptop is still usable.

items.title: Cabinet duo trade suits for running shoes
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari took part in the run. Fahmi said: "Thank you to Kelab Media Prima for organising the run. Present at the flag-off were Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor and New Straits Times group editor Datuk Farrah Naz Karim, NST deputy group editor Sharanjit Singh and Television Networks News and Current Affairs group editor Datuk Azhari Muhidin.

items.title: Nestle Malaysia supports padi farmers to boost supply chain
items.summary: JITRA: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has invested more than RM6 million in its Nestle Paddy Club (NPC) since 2012, as it seeks to strengthen its local rice supply chain while improving productivity and the livelihood of padi farmers. Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the investment also covers farming methods, agricultural inputs, machinery and technical expertise. "Some farmers also take out padi insurance.

items.title: Argentina revives naval base plans
items.summary: USHUAIA: Along the Beagle Channel, an icy stretch of water at the southern tip of the Americas, lies the dormant site of the proposed Ushuaia naval base. Earlier this month, right-wing President Javier Milei ordered that priority be given in Argentina's 2027 budget to the development of the base. Milei, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has previously championed development of the base in the context of Argentina's alignment with Washington.

items.title: Anwar bestowed Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award
items.summary: KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has received the inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of more than five decades of public service and contributions to education, Islamic scholarship, institutional development, international dialogue and human well-being. The manuscript was presented by India's Grand Mufti, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad. In a citation read during the ceremony, Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Rector Dr Roshan Nurani said Anwar had demonstrated perseverance, institutional vision and a sustained commitment to dialogue, equitable development, education and human dignity throughout his public life.

items.title: Man prepares more than 100 cash-filled envelopes before death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 100 envelopes containing cash prepared by an elderly man before his death became his final trust for his family to distribute to those who helped with his funeral arrangements. His granddaughter, Siti Mahirah Azemi, 30, said her grandfather, Yob Abd Karim, 93, appeared to have prepared himself for death and had set aside the money to be used when the time came. Siti Mahirah said her grandfather had appeared ready to leave and had often said before his death that his time was near.

items.title: 'I thought she was alone,' says sister of fish pond electrocution victim
items.summary: BESUT: Wan Affida Malina Wan Awang rushed to a fish farm pond in Pantai Air Tawar here after being told that her sister, Wan Adilah, had become unconscious, believed to have suffered an electric shock. Wan Affida Malina said she was informed about the incident by a family acquaintance at 1.07pm. She said her sister, Wan Adilah, 49, was the third of seven siblings and had been managing the fish farm since 2019.

items.title: Anwar meets India Grand Mufti in Kerala
items.summary: KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met prominent Sunni Muslim cleric and Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad at Jamia Markaz here, as Malaysia seeks to deepen religious, educational and economic ties with southern India. The prime minister later visited the Madavoor C.M. Keralam Chief Minister V.D.

items.title: Viral Cyberjaya barrier video: Police explain traffic policeman's actions
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: A traffic policeman captured in a viral video pushing open an automatic barrier at Tamarind Square did so only after receiving permission from the premises' management, police said. Sepang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the incident occurred about 2.30pm on Saturday when personnel from the district police Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division were escorting the official convoy of Datuk Undang Luak Johol. He said the convoy was travelling from the Serenia Toll Plaza towards Tamarind Square when the automatic barrier leading to the upper-level access road failed to open.

items.title: Hundreds flee Croatia island fire
items.summary: Authorities sounded the alarm shortly before midnight as flames threatened to get close to homes in the small town of Milna in the west of the island. Fanned by strong winds, the fire has consumed some 3,500 hectares, an area roughly two-thirds of Manhattan, authorities said. Two people have been wounded, including one seriously, firefighters told the official Hina news agency.

items.title: Former minister Jamil Khir to face three charges over Tabung Haji probe tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom is reportedly set to be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow in connection with an investigation into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) arising from a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). According to Bernama , the court system showed that Jamil Khir is scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad at 9am. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said on Thursday that the commission had recommended three charges against the former minister under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.

items.title: MOH assures healthcare access will continue in rural Sarawak after suspension of Flying Doctor Service
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has assured that access to healthcare services for rural communities in Sarawak will continue following the temporary suspension of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in the state. In a statement today, MOH said the suspension involved seven FDS teams covering 85 locations with an estimated population of 14,830 people in remote areas. “To ensure continuity of treatment, MOH is reassessing healthcare service programmes for each location based on accessibility and local conditions.

items.title: Parliament Open Day draws record 13,368 visitors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The two-day Parliament Open Day which began yesterday successfully attracted over 13,368 visitors, exceeding the initial target of 10,000 people. Parliament staff brief visitors inside the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara on the final day of the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026. Visitors take a closer look at the Parliament lobby during the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast in seven states and KL until 9pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 9pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said other areas affected are in Kedah (Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Baling and Sik) and Perak (Hulu Perak, Selama and Muallim). The same warning has been issued for Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, while in Terengganu, the areas involved are Hulu Terengganu, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Besut.

items.title: Anwar: No country should have to choose between repaying debt and caring for its people
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a fairer global financing system, saying no country should be forced to choose between repaying its debts and meeting its obligations to its people. “No nation should be forced to choose between honouring its debts and honouring its obligations to its people,” he said when delivering his speech at the National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the end of the 18th Brics Leaders Summit here today. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said financing must be “fit for purpose”, stressing that meeting basic needs and providing public goods should not leave countries with unsustainable debt.

items.title: Man hospitalised after unknown assailant stabs him at KL Wholesale Market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — A man in his 30s was injured in the back after being stabbed with a sharp metal object by an unidentified individual at the Kuala Lumpur Wholesale Market yesterday. Sentul acting district police chief Supt Jasni Zolpa said the incident occurred at about 8.40am while the man was working at the market. The victim's friend also lodged a police report about the incident at 1.30pm today.

items.title: ‘This may be my last time’: Abang Johari hints at possible final term as PBB president, calls on younger leaders to step up
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 13 — “This may be my last time.” That was the candid message from Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg as he called on the older generation to make way for younger leaders to carry on the responsibility and struggle of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB). The PBB president said leadership succession was a natural process and that the party must continuously prepare and train younger members to take over when the time came.

items.title: Anglers find barrel with suspected human remains near Machap Water Reservoir
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 13 — A barrel believed to contain human remains was found on a slope by the roadside near the Machap Water Reservoir here today, according to Alor Gajah police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar. He said the blue barrel was found by three anglers aged between 25 and 35 while fishing at the reservoir at about 11.40am. Ahmad said initial investigations found that the remains were believed to have been decomposing for at least three weeks.

items.title: Anwar heads to Keralam for final leg of India visit after Brics summit
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for India’s Southern State, Keralam (renamed from Kerala) for his second and final leg of his working visit in India after participating in the 18th Brics’ Leaders Summit here. The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister departed the Air Force Station (AFS) Palam, New Delhi at 2.15pm local time (4.45pm Malaysian Time) to Kozhikode (Calicut), Keralam. As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet the Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Kerala Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar.

items.title: Home minister: New deputy IGP chosen after consultation with King, announcement due soon
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 13 — The appointment of the new deputy inspector-general of police (IGP) has been finalised and will be announced soon, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution said several names had been considered and discussions held before the process was finalised. On the eligibility criteria for the deputy IGP post, Saifuddin Nasution said all officers holding the rank of police commissioner (CP) were eligible for consideration.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for unity to counter PAS and Umno’s racial, religious politics
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has called on Malaysians to unite against what he described as the “dangerous brand of extremist politics” projected by PAS and Umno following their respective party gatherings. In a written statement today, Lim said the conclusion of the PAS Muktamar and Umno General Assembly had projected politics centred on religious and racial dominance without respecting the “basic spirit and fundamental tenets” of the Federal Constitution and the rule of law. Lim proposed 10 areas that he said could help counter PAS and Umno while fostering national unity in Malaysia’s multiracial society and greater integration between Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Kota Bharu police seek man seen kicking young girl in restaurant CCTV video
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Police have opened an investigation paper in connection with a viral video showing a man kicking a young girl at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot here. Kota Bharu police chief ACP Mohd Azmir Damiri said police received a report from a member of the public at about 10.24pm today regarding the video, which went viral on the Threads social media platform. “The video shows the rough behaviour of a man kicking a young girl believed to be his daughter at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot.

items.title: Malaysia’s Brics partnership broadens trade ties while keeping ‘middle path’, says J-KOM
items.summary: GOPENG, Sept 13 — Malaysia’s participation as a Brics partner opens up wider trade opportunities with member countries that collectively represent more than half of the world’s population and purchasing power. “With Brics, we can balance our trade with various other countries. “The 11 Brics member countries are official members.

items.title: FDS crash: Dr Ainul’s husband thanks all, calls nationwide support a ‘blessing’
items.summary: Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, said the support from the federal, Sarawak and Kelantan governments had greatly helped facilitate arrangements concerning his late wife, including throughout his time in Sarawak. Thank you to everyone, including the media,” he told reporters when met at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here today. Dr Ainul Baraah, 33, was laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery at 2.20pm today following funeral prayers at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa.

items.title: MOH to review all FDS helicopter contracts, RM30 flight allowance after fatal Sarawak crash
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will review all contracts related to helicopter services for the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following the crash of an FDS helicopter in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak, last Tuesday. Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said the review would cover all aspects of the contracts, including matters related to FDS, in line with instructions from Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. Following the crash, MOH announced that FDS operations in Sarawak would be temporarily suspended to allow a comprehensive assessment of the service's safety and operational mechanisms.

items.title: EC to review electoral boundaries nationwide if Parliament approves more Sabah, Sarawak seats
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Election Commission (EC) will conduct a review of electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said it took note of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement on Friday on the proposed amendments to the Federal Constitution to allow for an increase in the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak. “In the context of the delineation of electoral constituencies in the three study units, the EC will conduct a review of the electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Police, RMAF among four agencies supporting Sarawak during Flying Doctor Service suspension
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Four enforcement agencies will assist the Ministry of Health (MOH) in carrying out mercy flights to aid people in remote areas of Sarawak who require medical assistance. The four agencies are the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), and the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM). “The mobilised alternatives include securing assistance from JBPM through its Emergency Medical Air Rescue Services (EMARS).

items.title: Anwar: 1MDB recovery about restoring trust amid RM4.2b claim against Singapore’s DBS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Finance (MoF) has taken note of a compensation claim amounting to approximately RM4.2 billion filed by four companies against DBS Bank Ltd at the Singapore High Court. The MoF statement also said that, according to the 1MDB Asset Recovery Task Force, the claim involves five DBS accounts opened in 2013 by the four companies. The accounts were allegedly used to channel more than US$1 billion (RM4.07 billion) in misappropriated 1MDB and SRC funds between 2013 and 2014.

items.title: Construction of Cameron Highlands bypass yet to begin, suspension calls premature, says Works Ministry
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) has taken note of media reports and concerns raised regarding flash floods and landslides in Cameron Highlands, including calls for the temporary suspension of the Cameron Highlands Bypass Project. In a statement today, the Public Works Department (JKR) explained that the project involves the construction of the Tanah Rata Bypass, the upgrading of Federal Road FT59 from Tanah Rata to Kea Farm, and the upgrading of Federal Road FT434 (Jalan Griddle). “Therefore, any claims linking the flash flood incident to the project's physical construction activities are inaccurate,” the statement read.

items.title: Health Minister leads funeral prayers for helicopter crash victim Dr Ainul Baraah
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today. The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased’s family members and friends. Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah’s remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.

items.title: Fisherman missing after falling into sea near Pulau Batu Layang found dead
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 13 — The body of a fisherman who fell into the sea while fishing near Pulau Batu Layang, Sungai Baru here yesterday, was found about 400 metres from the island today. Kuala Perlis Maritime Zone director Maritime Commander Nak Rong A/L Si Prom said the body was discovered by local fishermen and the finding was reported to the search and rescue operation team this morning. “The operation team received information from the fishing community about the discovery of a body approximately 400 metres from Pulau Batu Layang,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Health Ministry preparing for possible rise in public hospital patients amid soaring insurance costs
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is constantly planning and projecting healthcare service requirements to prepare for a possible increase in the number of patients at public hospitals amid rising health insurance costs. Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said such planning and projections formed part of the public healthcare sector’s day-to-day and long-term planning, including financial requirements to meet changes in demand for healthcare services. Dr Mahathar said the ministry was also aware of concerns over reported increases of up to 20 per cent annually in health insurance costs, which could place a greater financial burden on the public and affect demand for public healthcare services.

items.title: Anwar confirms Malaysia exploring acquisition of India’s BrahMos missile system
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia is exploring the possibility of acquiring India’s BrahMos air-to-surface missile system, while emphasising that discussions are still ongoing and no final decision has been made. In an interview with India’s NDTV, he said discussion on it took place during the bilateral meeting with his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, but the rightful decision maker would be Malaysia’s Air Force. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, acknowledged India’s defence capabilities.

items.title: Teen among 146 detained in road bully operation at Bukit Raja toll plaza
items.summary: Sinar Harian reported that the integrated operation involving the Selangor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT), Road Transport Department (JPJ) and National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) also resulted in 50 motorcycles being seized for various offences. In a statement, Selangor police said 146 individuals aged between 16 and 25, as well as 141 motorcycles, were inspected during the operation. “Selangor police issued 92 summonses, while the Bukit Aman JSPT issued 24 summonses for various traffic offences,” the statement said.
